summary: Backend-only test of P0 Account Lockout Security. Wrote /app/backend/tests/test_account_lockout.py (13 tests) exercising POST /api/auth/login lockout flow, GET /api/auth/lockout-status, POST /api/auth/unlock-account (invalid + valid token), GET /api/auth/admin/locked-accounts (auth guard + listing + PII projection), POST /api/auth/admin/unlock-account/{email} (success + not-found + auth guard), and the account_locked email template + URL construction. 12/13 pass, 1 skipped (login-while-locked pre-check test hits the 5/min IP rate-limit after the 5-attempt trigger — behavioural interaction between the /login rate limit and the lockout trigger; not a defect). Found and fixed one real 500 bug in account_lockout_service.unlock_with_token (timezone-naive vs aware datetime comparison) that made the email-token unlock flow crash for every user.

critical.issue: 500 TypeError: can't compare offset-naive and offset-aware datetimes in AccountLockoutService.unlock_with_token when comparing `now > token_expires` — MongoDB returns naive datetime while `now` is UTC-aware. Every real user clicking the unlock link would have hit this 500. FIXED in this iteration by mirroring the tz normalization already used in check_lockout_status (see updated_files).

minor.issue: The /login endpoint's IP rate limit is 5/minute (security_middleware.RATE_LIMITS['login']) which is exactly the lockout threshold. This means the very same request that triggers lockout (5th attempt) also exhausts the rate window, so ANY subsequent /login call within the next minute (including from a legitimate user on the same NAT/proxy IP) returns 429 instead of the intended 423 account_locked. Consider raising the login rate limit to 6-10/min so the 423 pre-check on line 174 of auth_routes.py can actually run for the immediate follow-up request.

No rate limit and no auth — allows account enumeration via timing/response differences (`remaining_attempts: 5` on unknown vs `locked: true` on known-locked). Low severity but worth a rate-limit + generic response for unknown emails.

record_failed_attempt is called for BOTH unknown emails and wrong passwords. This causes a DB row (account_lockouts) to be inserted for any email an attacker probes, which is fine for security but note it also enables a trivial DoS: an attacker can lock any known user email by making 5 wrong-password attempts. Consider adding a CAPTCHA / IP-based throttle before failed-attempt recording, or exponential backoff.

action_items: Review + keep the tz fix in services/account_lockout_service.py::unlock_with_token (lines ~214-219). Consider adding the same guard everywhere Mongo datetimes are compared to `now` (e.g. account_lockouts.lockout_until — currently handled in check_lockout_status only).

Raise the /login rate limit above the 5-attempt lockout threshold (e.g. 10/min) so the 423 pre-check in auth_routes.login (lines 172-183) actually returns account_locked instead of 429 for the very next request after lockout.
Add a lightweight rate-limit + generic response to GET /api/auth/lockout-status to close the account-enumeration side channel.

P0 asks include a frontend UnlockAccountPage.js & PDFDocumentViewer.js and P2 asks for CRM component exports — these were NOT tested per review request ('testing_type: backend only'). Main agent should trigger a frontend test iteration after the /login rate-limit fix ships.
critical_code_review_comments: account_lockout_service.unlock_with_token had NO tz normalization for unlock_token_expires — direct copy-paste of the pattern in check_lockout_status (lines 176-180) was missing. This was a guaranteed 500 for every legitimate unlock-link click. Fixed.

auth_routes.login builds the 423 detail with `remaining_seconds // 60` (line 179) which floors to 0 when <60s remain, giving the user 'Try again in 0 minutes' — prefer max(1, seconds//60) or show seconds.

account_lockout_service.record_failed_attempt records failed attempts for non-existent users too. Combined with the 5-attempt lock this is a targeted DoS vector against ANY known email (competitor locks CEO out for 30 min repeatedly). Consider only recording after the user actually exists, or require CAPTCHA after 3 attempts.

auth_routes.get_lockout_status shadows the imported `status` module with a local variable named `status` on line 707 — subtle but risks future refactors (e.g. adding `status.HTTP_400_BAD_REQUEST` in that function will NameError).

auth_routes.login: the 423 pre-check (line 174) blocks the request BEFORE incrementing failed_attempts, but the /login rate limit (5/min) will 429 first for the same IP window that caused the lock. Net effect: 423 pre-check is unreachable in practice.
AccountLockoutService.get_locked_accounts projects out `unlock_token` and `_id` — verified in test. Good.
updated_files: /app/backend/services/account_lockout_service.py (added tz-aware normalization for unlock_token_expires in unlock_with_token — fixes 500 bug)

success_rate.backend: 92.3% (12/13, 1 skipped due to /login rate-limit interaction — see minor issues)

context_for_next_testing_agent: Account lockout backend is functional end-to-end after the unlock_with_token tz fix. Test file test_account_lockout.py needs the 60-65s sleep between runs because it consumes the full 5/min /login window per run — if you rerun immediately, TestAccountLockoutFlow::test_five_failed_attempts_lock_account and test_login_while_locked_returns_423 will skip. Frontend pieces (UnlockAccountPage.js, PDFDocumentViewer.js, CRM component exports) were explicitly out of scope this iteration — request frontend testing next.
rca_of_the_issue: unlock_with_token read unlock_token_expires from MongoDB, which returns a NAIVE datetime, then compared it to datetime.now(timezone.utc) (aware). Python raises TypeError. The sibling function check_lockout_status already had the tz-normalization pattern (lines 176-180) but it was not applied here. Repro before fix: trigger lockout for any user → get unlock_token from db.account_lockouts → POST /api/auth/unlock-account with valid email+token → 500 Internal Server Error, backend.err.log shows the TypeError at services/account_lockout_service.py line 220. Fix: add `elif token_expires and token_expires.tzinfo is None: token_expires = token_expires.replace(tzinfo=timezone.utc)` right after the isinstance-str branch. Verified: the same unlock request now returns 200 {success: true, message: 'Account unlocked successfully'} and db.account_lockouts reflects locked=false, unlocked_via='email_token'.
